key_insight: A continuous finite element method achieves second-order accuracy for scalar conservation laws with fractional diffusion while preserving a discrete maximum principle.
engineering_relevance: The method supports physically bounded simulations of anomalous transport and nonlocal diffusion on unstructured meshes.
method: Approximate the fractional Laplacian using sinc quadrature and finite element resolvent solves.
Combine graph viscosity with explicit SSP Runge–Kutta integration for a monotone baseline.
Apply entropy-consistent corrections and convex limiting for maximum-principle-preserving second-order accuracy.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments, including Surface Quasi-Geostrophic applications, confirm second-order accuracy and robustness on unstructured meshes.
watch_item: Maximum-principle preservation requires an explicit CFL restriction, while fractional diffusion introduces multiple resolvent solves.
paper_title: Maximum principle preserving approximation of scalar conservation equations with a fractional Laplacian
